title: How repositioning from "save money" to "create growth" lets you charge 8x for the same product
summary: Jason Cohen argues that pricing is driven by positioning and perceived value, not cost analysis. Using a hypothetical AdWords tool, he shows that a "generate growth" pitch is worth a multiple of a "save money" pitch, both in value created and in the share of it customers will pay. Frame your product in the way your customer already measures value.

principles.text: Pricing depends on positioning and perceived value, not cost analysis or ROI calculators.
principles.quote: Pricing is much more about positioning and perceived value than it is about cost-analysis and unconvincing ROI calculators.

principles.text: A business values growing faster about 10x more than saving money, so sell growth.
principles.quote: It's always 10x more valuable for a business to grow faster than it is for the business to save money.

principles.text: Under a savings pitch you can only charge a fraction of the savings, because the customer must keep most of the value.
principles.quote: In the "saves money" pitch, the value was $20,000, and the customer needed to keep 75% of that value-creation.

principles.text: Under a growth pitch the customer will pay all of the value created, since the extra spend buys more growth at a similar unit cost.
principles.quote: in the "generate growth" pitch, the value is $40,000, and the customer is happy to pay 100% of that value-creation to a vendor.

principles.text: Repositioning raises both the value created and the share the customer will pay, so price rises by a multiple.
principles.quote: Both the amount of value created, and the percentage of value the customer is willing to pay, is a multiple higher for the "growth" pitch versus the "save money" pitch.

principles.text: Don't pitch saving time, money or efficiency; tie the product to how the customer already measures value.
principles.quote: figure out how your product creates value in the way your customer already measures value, and position your product as a way to accomplish that.
